Install from the browser experimental

The same installer as the command-line one, run from Chrome or Edge over USB. Nothing to install on the computer.

Experimental: not yet tested on a real Brick. This page runs exactly the device-side steps of the command-line installer, but its USB path has so far been tested only against a simulated Brick. Until that changes, the command-line installer is the recommended way.

This replaces your Brick's operating system. The boot and root partitions are overwritten by Amalthea Linux; the stock system is copied to your computer first. You do this at your own risk, with no warranty of any kind (GNU GPL v3, sections 15 and 16). Not affiliated with or endorsed by TRIMUI.

What you need

  • A TRIMUI Brick (TG3040) on the stock firmware, charged to at least 50 %, and a USB-C data cable.
  • Chrome or Edge on macOS, Windows, Linux or ChromeOS (WebUSB and folder access; Firefox and Safari have neither).
  • About 600 MB free on the computer. No other program may be using ADB: if Android platform-tools are installed, run adb kill-server first.
  • Windows: the Google USB Driver if Windows has no driver for the Brick's ADB interface. Linux: the android-udev-rules package (USB vendor 18d1).

Installing

  1. Download the installer archive. Latest release: github.com/nzimas/amalthea/releases/latest. Do not unzip it. Then choose it here:

    (no archive chosen)

  2. Switch the Brick on, let the stock system start, and connect it to the computer with the USB-C cable.

  3. The browser asks you to choose the Brick (it is listed as an ADB device) and, on a stock Brick, a folder for the stock backup: it is saved there as backup-<serial>. Keep that folder; it is how you go back to stock. On a Brick that already runs Amalthea (on its home screen), the same button updates it and first copies your saved sessions to the folder.

Going back to the stock system

Choose the installer archive above, connect the Brick (Amalthea on its home screen) and press . If the Brick no longer holds its copy of the backup, the page asks for the folder with backup-<serial>.

What is not known yet

The steps on the Brick are those of the command-line installer, run by the same script. What only a real Brick can show:

  • whether the stock firmware's ADB daemon accepts the browser's connection (the USB interface, and authentication, if it asks for it);
  • how fast the 515 MB backup comes over WebUSB with the old daemon's 4 KB packets;
  • whether, after the restart, the browser still has permission for the Brick running Amalthea. If it has not, the page asks you to choose it again.

If anything goes wrong, nothing is lost that the command-line installer cannot recover: it reads the same state on the Brick. Please report problems on GitHub with the log shown above.
